_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH. Every string shown on the House Rules screen comes from this file. Views must contain zero literal rule text. If a string is not in this file, it does not appear in the app.

constants._readme: These values are read by BOTH the scoring engine and the House Rules screen. Never duplicate them anywhere else.

streakRescue._monthlyTokenNote: Product override of lifetime first-free: 1 Rescue token per member per calendar month.

conditions._readme: Closed enum. Cursor implements ONE resolver function isVisible(conditionKey, household) -> Bool with exactly these cases plus null. Do NOT build an expression parser or accept arbitrary strings.
conditions.ALLOWANCE_ON: household.rewardModel is one of: allowance, xp_allowance, full_system
conditions.REWARDS_ON: household.rewardModel is one of: xp_rewards, full_system
conditions.XP_ON: household.rewardModel is one of: xp_only, xp_rewards, xp_allowance, full_system

phases._readme: Closed enum, used by Direction 03 (The Track) to place a rule. EVERY rule must declare exactly one. Build fails if any rule has a phase outside this list. 'anytime' is the catch-all so a new rule can never be unplaceable.

visuals._readme: Closed enum, used by Direction 02 (At a glance). 'none' renders the quiet outlined card. Data for each visual comes from constants above — never hardcode the numbers into the component.
visuals.xpRamp: Six ascending bars labelled from constants.xpValues.
visuals.dayTimeline: Single rail, three markers at 7:00 PM / late window / 11:59 PM.
visuals.streakDots: Seven dots, first two filled, from constants.streak.
visuals.modelList: Five rows from constants.rewardModels, household's active model highlighted.

adult.headline: Value follows difficulty
adult.question: How much is a task worth?
adult.clause: Every task carries an XP value from 5 to 30, set by difficulty. Finish before the deadline and the full value is awarded.

kid.headline: Every job is worth points
kid.question: How many points do I get?
kid.body: Small jobs are worth 5 and the biggest ones are worth 30. Finish on time, get all of them.

adult.headline: The bundle bonus
adult.question: What's the bundle bonus?
adult.clause: Finish every task in a domain group on time for a +10 XP bundle bonus. If any task in it ran late, the bonus is +7.

kid.headline: Finish a whole set, get a bonus
kid.question: What's a bundle bonus?
kid.body: All the jobs in one group, done on time — that's 10 extra. If one was late, it's 7.

adult.headline: XP lands on Complete
adult.question: When does XP actually land?
adult.clause: XP lands the moment a kid taps Complete — not on approval. You're notified and can verify afterward.

kid.headline: Points show up right away
kid.question: Do I have to wait for my points?
kid.body: Tap Complete and they're yours. You don't have to wait for anyone.

adult.headline: Hygiene builds streaks, not points
adult.question: Why did a task score zero?
adult.clause: Personal Hygiene tasks are tracked as streaks, not points. 19 of the 150 library tasks score zero XP by design.

kid.headline: Hygiene jobs are different
kid.question: Why did brushing my teeth give me nothing?
kid.body: Hygiene jobs don't pay points on purpose. They build your streak instead — and the streak is the hard one to get.

adult.headline: Admins only
adult.question: Who can assign and approve?
adult.clause: Only admins can assign tasks, approve completions, request proof, and approve allowance.

kid.headline: A parent sets your list
kid.question: Who assigns my jobs?
kid.body: Only an admin can give out jobs, check them off, ask for a photo or approve allowance.

adult.headline: When everything is due
adult.question: When is everything due?
adult.clause: Daily tasks close at 7:00 PM household time. Weekly tasks close Sunday 7:00 PM, monthly on the last Sunday at 7:00 PM.

kid.headline: The bell rings at 7:00 PM
kid.question: When do I have to be done?
kid.body: Weekly jobs are due Sunday. Monthly ones on the last Sunday.

adult.headline: Poppins reminds
adult.question: Does anyone get warned?
adult.clause: Poppins sends task notifications, including a final nudge 30 minutes before anything is due.

kid.headline: Poppins warns you first
kid.question: Will I get a reminder?
kid.body: You get a nudge 30 minutes before anything is due.

adult.headline: Late Credit
adult.question: They finished at 8 PM — what did they lose?
adult.clause: Late Credit is applied the instant Complete is tapped, and never recomputed. A late task still keeps the streak and carries a late indicator.

kid.headline: Late still counts
kid.question: What if I'm late?
kid.body: You still get points, just a few less. A 10 turns into a 7. Your streak stays safe, so it's always worth finishing.

adult.headline: The day closes
adult.question: Can they still do yesterday's task?
adult.clause: At 11:59 PM anything unfinished becomes Expired and can no longer be completed.

kid.headline: At 11:59 PM the day closes
kid.question: How late is too late?
kid.body: Anything left is gone. Tomorrow is a fresh list.

adult.headline: Weekly and monthly are safer
adult.question: Does a missed weekly task break the streak?
adult.clause: An expired weekly or monthly task costs its XP but never breaks a streak.

kid.headline: Weekly jobs can't hurt your streak
kid.question: Does missing a weekly job break my streak?
kid.body: You lose the points, but the streak keeps going.

adult.headline: What feeds a streak
adult.question: Which tasks count toward a streak?
adult.clause: Only daily and weekday tasks feed the streak.

kid.headline: Daily jobs keep it alive
kid.question: How do I keep my streak?
kid.body: Weekly and monthly jobs can't break it, ever.

adult.headline: Three misses and it's over
adult.question: What breaks a streak?
adult.clause: A streak ends after 3 misses in a row, or 3 misses inside any rolling 7 days.

kid.headline: Three misses ends it
kid.question: What breaks my streak?
kid.body: Three days in a row, or three days in one week.

adult.headline: What a save costs
adult.question: What does Streak Rescue cost?
adult.clause: Streak Rescue costs 10% of that week's XP after one missed day and 20% after two consecutive. A third consecutive miss loses the streak permanently. Decline and the XP stays, the streak goes.

kid.headline: You can buy a day back
kid.question: Can I save my streak?
kid.body: One missed day costs 10% of the week's points. Two costs 20%. After three, the streak is gone for good.

adult.headline: Pause without losing ground
adult.question: What happens when we travel?
adult.clause: Recess switches tasks off and freezes streaks at their current value — leave on 12 days, return on 12 days.

kid.headline: Recess pauses everything
kid.question: What if we go on holiday?
kid.body: On holiday your streak waits for you. Leave on 12 days, come back on 12 days.

adult.headline: The Week's Crown
adult.question: How is the weekly winner decided?
adult.clause: The Week's Crown goes to the highest XP each week. Monthly Sovereign is settled on the last Sunday.

kid.headline: The Week's Crown
kid.question: How do I win a crown?
kid.body: Most points in the week wins it. The last Sunday of the month decides the Monthly Sovereign.

adult.headline: Gold, silver, bronze
adult.question: How are places shown?
adult.clause: First place is gold, second silver, third bronze.

kid.headline: Gold, silver, bronze
kid.question: What do the colours mean?
kid.body: First place is gold, second is silver, third is bronze.

adult.headline: Ties share a rank
adult.question: What if two kids tie?
adult.clause: Ties produce duplicate ranks — two firsts, then two seconds.

kid.headline: A tie means you both win
kid.question: What if we tie?
kid.body: Same points, same place. Nobody gets bumped down.

adult.headline: Every sheet is open
adult.question: What's on the winner's sheet?
adult.clause: The winner's sheet shows tasks completed, on-time count and late tasks. Every member's sheet is viewable.

kid.headline: You can see everyone's week
kid.question: Can I see how everyone did?
kid.body: The sheet shows jobs finished, how many were on time, and how many were late. Everyone's is open.

adult.headline: Champion's Record
adult.question: Where do past wins live?
adult.clause: Champion's Record keeps every crown won, by member.

kid.headline: Your Champion's Record
kid.question: Where do my old wins go?
kid.body: Every crown you've ever won is kept there. So are everyone else's.

adult.headline: Trophies run on lifetime XP
adult.question: How do trophies work?
adult.clause: Trophies unlock on lifetime XP. The top tier, Most Glorious, sits at 100,000 XP.

kid.headline: Trophies never reset
kid.question: What's a trophy?
kid.body: Trophies come from all the points you've ever earned. The biggest one is Most Glorious, at 100,000.

adult.headline: How this household rewards
adult.question: What can we reward with?
adult.clause: The household runs one of five models: XP only, Allowance, XP + Rewards, XP + Allowance, or the full system.

kid.headline: How your prizes work
kid.question: What do I get for finishing?
kid.body: Your family picks how prizes work — points, allowance, real rewards, or all of it together.

adult.headline: Rewards follow the day
adult.question: What earns a reward?
adult.clause: Rewards are tied to finishing that day's assigned tasks and homework. Each reward carries its own frequency.

kid.headline: Prizes come from finishing the day
kid.question: How do I earn a prize?
kid.body: Your tasks and your homework. Your family chooses what the prize is.

adult.headline: Instant or approved
adult.question: Does a reward need my approval?
adult.clause: A reward is either instant or requires approval, set per reward.

kid.headline: Some prizes need a yes first
kid.question: Do I get a prize right away?
kid.body: Some are instant. Others wait for a parent to say yes.

adult.headline: Recorded, not transferred
adult.question: Does ChoreMaxx send the money?
adult.clause: Allowance is recorded in ChoreMaxx, not transferred — no money moves through the app. Approvals follow the household schedule, and Approve now always works.

kid.headline: Allowance is counted here
kid.question: When do I get my allowance?
kid.body: ChoreMaxx keeps the score. The actual money comes from your family.

adult.headline: Mint Reward
adult.question: Can I make my own reward?
adult.clause: Mint Reward creates one of your own, on any reward page.

kid.headline: Your family can invent prizes
kid.question: Can we make up our own prize?
kid.body: Any prize you can think of can be added to the list.

adult.headline: Verify without gating
adult.question: Can I check they actually did it?
adult.clause: On chores, admins can request proof on a completed task. It's optional and per task — it verifies the work, it doesn't gate the reward.

kid.headline: A parent might ask for a photo
kid.question: Why do I need a photo?
kid.body: Only on chores you've already finished. It's a check, not a test.

adult.headline: Homework proof is required
adult.question: How does homework proof work?
adult.clause: Homework keeps its own tab, and photo proof is required. It's configured per child, on by default, and an admin confirms it.

kid.headline: Homework needs a photo
kid.question: Do I have to photograph my homework?
kid.body: Snap it when you're done so a parent can check it off.

adult.headline: Admins and Helpers
adult.question: What can a Helper do?
adult.clause: Two roles: Admin and Helper. Helpers complete their own tasks and see their own record — everything in the admin list stays with admins.

kid.headline: You're a Helper
kid.question: What can I do?
kid.body: You finish your own jobs and see your own record and crowns.

adult.headline: These rules are yours
adult.question: Can I change these rules?
adult.clause: Admins can change any rule here. The kid version rewrites itself to match, in their words.

kid.headline: Rules can change
kid.question: Can rules change?
kid.body: If a parent changes something, this page updates too. Check back if the house feels different.

footnotes.adult: Deadlines run on household-local time. Rule changes take effect the next day, so nothing already in progress changes value mid-task.
